title: Non-geometrically reduced fibres near a non-geometrically reduced generic fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $Y$ is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and suppose the generic fibre $X_\eta$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is not geometrically reduced over $\kappa(\eta)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that for every $y\in V$, the fibre $X_y$ is not geometrically reduced over $\kappa(y)$. No flatness, reducedness of $Y$, Noetherianity, or nonemptiness of the fibres is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-generic-geometrically-reduced-preparation] to the given finite type $f:X\to Y$ with irreducible base $Y$. It supplies a nonempty open $U\subseteq Y$, an integral affine scheme $T$, and a finite universal homeomorphism $q:T\to U$. Use the composite $T\xrightarrow{q}U\hookrightarrow Y$ to form $P=X\times_YT$, with projection $h:P\to T$, and $R=P_{\mathrm{red}}$. By [def-pc-integral-scheme], $T$ is nonempty and irreducible. Apply [lem-sc-scheme-sober] to the irreducible closed subset $T$ of itself to choose its generic point $\xi$. Preparation says that $R_\xi$ is geometrically reduced over $\kappa(\xi)$.

Apply [lem-trf-prepared-generic-fibre-nonreduced] with the original $f,Y,\eta$ and the diagram $U,T,q,P,R$ of step 1, using the same composite $T\xrightarrow{q}U\hookrightarrow Y$ in its fibre product. Its finite type and irreducible-base hypotheses are the original ones; $U$ is nonempty, $T$ integral with generic point $\xi$, and $q$ a universal homeomorphism by step 1. The original hypothesis gives that $X_\eta$ is not geometrically reduced, while preparation gives that $R_\xi$ is geometrically reduced. The lemma therefore gives that $P_\xi$ is not reduced.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-universal-homeomorphism-nonreduced-fibre-spreading] with the same $f,U,T,q,\xi$ and the same $Y$-scheme structure on $T$. Its hypotheses hold: $f$ is finite type by the original assumption; $U$ is an open subscheme of $Y$, $T$ is irreducible with generic point $\xi$, and $q:T\to U$ is a universal homeomorphism by step 1; the fibre $P_\xi$ is not reduced by step 2. The lemma supplies a nonempty open $W\subseteq T$ for which $V=q(W)\subseteq U\subseteq Y$ is nonempty and open in $Y$, and $X_y$ is not geometrically reduced over $\kappa(y)$ for every $y\in V$. Taking this image $V$ proves the conclusion.
